headline: Maker Creates 64-bit USB Drive Using 1950s Tech
summary: Polymatt builds a USB drive with 64 bits of storage using magnetic core memory
details: Polymatt, a maker, has created a USB drive with 64 bits of storage using magnetic core memory, an ancient technology from the 1950s. The device uses 64 iron rings, each storing a single bit, and is immersed in silicon oil for aesthetic purposes.

The maker salvaged tiny magnetic rings from an old Russian computer to build the device, which offers persistent, unpowered storage and can withstand radiation bursts that would damage modern memory devices.

The DIY memory device can store a single persistent file called core.txt and has been tested to demonstrate its non-volatile capabilities. The project showcases an alternative approach to modern memory solutions.
caption:
